title: Add a batch upload queue with a concurrency limit, one retry and abort
prompt:
Add a batch upload queue as a new feature directory src/main/features/uploads. Its index.ts exports createBatchUploader and nothing else.

createBatchUploader(deps: UploadDeps) returns an object { uploadAll }. The deps parameter has the type { readonly upload: (batch: readonly Item[], signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<void>; readonly sleep: (ms: number) => Promise<void>; readonly now: () => number }, where an Item is { readonly id: string }. The feature does no I/O and sets no timers of its own: it uploads only through deps.upload, waits only through deps.sleep and reads the clock only through deps.now.

uploadAll(items: readonly Item[], options: { readonly batchSize: number; readonly concurrency: number; readonly signal: AbortSignal }): Promise<UploadSummary> uploads the items in batches. The rules:

Batches. The items are split, in order, into consecutive batches of batchSize items; the last batch may be smaller. Batch i (counting from 0) has index i. No items means no batches.

Options. batchSize and concurrency must be positive integers. Otherwise the returned promise rejects with a RangeError whose message is 'batchSize must be a positive integer' or 'concurrency must be a positive integer' (batchSize is checked first), before any dep is called and whatever the items and the signal are. A concurrency larger than the number of batches is valid, however large.

Concurrency. A batch is in progress from its first deps.upload call until it is uploaded or given up, including the wait before its retry. At most options.concurrency batches are in progress at once. Batches start in index order: as soon as a batch stops being in progress, the unstarted batch with the lowest index starts, and at the beginning the first min(concurrency, number of batches) batches start without waiting for one another. Starting a batch means calling deps.upload(batch, options.signal), with exactly those two arguments, where batch holds that batch's items in order. Two uploadAll calls running at the same time on one uploader are independent, each with its own limit.

Retry. If deps.upload rejects (with any value) or throws synchronously, the batch waits with deps.sleep(1000), once, with exactly that value, and then deps.upload is called again for the same batch with the same arguments. If that second attempt resolves, the batch is uploaded. If it rejects or throws, the batch is given up as failed: there is no third attempt, and the other batches carry on. deps.now() is read exactly once for each failed batch, right after its second attempt failed, and nowhere else.

Abort. Before it starts a batch (the first ones included), uploadAll checks options.signal.aborted. Once the signal is aborted, no batch that has not started ever starts. A batch that has started always runs to its end: an abort does not cancel its upload, its wait or its retry. uploadAll resolves only after every batch that started has finished. Nothing is listened to on the signal; it is only passed to deps.upload.

Summary. The promise resolves to an UploadSummary: { readonly kind: 'done'; readonly uploaded: number; readonly failedBatches: readonly FailedBatch[] } when every batch started (this includes an empty list of items, even with an aborted signal), or { readonly kind: 'aborted'; readonly uploaded: number; readonly failedBatches: readonly FailedBatch[]; readonly notStarted: readonly Item[] } when at least one batch never started. uploaded is the number of items (not batches) in the batches that were uploaded, whether on the first attempt or the retry. A FailedBatch is { readonly index: number; readonly items: readonly Item[]; readonly reason: string; readonly failedAt: number }, where items are the batch's items, reason is the message of the Error that the second attempt rejected with (String(value) for any other rejected or thrown value) and failedAt is the value deps.now() returned. failedBatches is ordered by batch index, whatever order the batches finished in. notStarted holds the items of the batches that never started, flattened, in their original order.

Do not change the greeting feature, and do not touch src/main/composition-root.ts. Add tests in test/uploads.test.ts for batching, the concurrency limit, retry, abort and the summaries, with fake deps whose upload promises the test controls: no real timers and no fixed sleeps. Run nitpicker-gate until it exits 0.
